If I could have given it 0 stars, I would have.
As soon as we walked in, the lady was arguing on the phone with a customer who was complaining that his dog had been attacked. To avoid being suspicious, I left my dog ​​anyway, asking ONLY for a wash and two additional services (detangling and intimate hygiene). The woman asked why she didn't cut him, and I repeatedly pointed out that the vet had absolutely said not to cut him until he was 9 months old, and he's 6. Same thing with nail trimming. When I went to pick him up, the dog was terrified and very sad, and he seemed different than usual; I almost didn't recognize him. I asked if they had cut him, and the woman said she had only cut the hair in front of his eyes. I said I had expressly told her not to touch him and to just wash him, and instead of apologizing, she said I shouldn't call her by her first name because we weren't friends! They continued to insist that the hair was too long and was going over his eyes. No empathy, no manners, no professionalism, nothing at all.

When asked for explanations, they make up a thousand reasons. The cleanliness doesn't seem exceptional because my dog ​​smelled damp after being bathed. My dog ​​bit the owner while she was trimming his nails. Probably inappropriately, because in five years, it's never happened anywhere else. The things that bothered me the most were the complete lack of empathy with dogs (yelling and screaming to keep them quiet) and the rudeness of the owner, who was yelling at a dissatisfied customer on the phone while I was waiting to pay. I'm not used to leaving negative reviews, but this time I can't help it.

Only after the service was I told that, for subsequent visits, I would have to bring him in the evening because in the morning he was "covered in hair." Despite this, the work they did was good, so I decided to give them a second chance.

For the second appointment, I scheduled a late afternoon appointment. After calling to confirm, the lady told me I would have to brush the dog before bringing him in due to excessive shedding. I found the request rather absurd, but I politely agreed anyway.

The same day of the appointment, she called me back, completely forgetting the phone call I'd had a few days earlier, to tell me that she only bathes large dogs in September and that she could only brush him.

At that point, I decided to go to another groomer. If you don't want or can't work with large dogs, it would be better not to advertise a service on your website that you're actually not willing to offer.
I won't be returning, and I don't recommend it.

Today I showed up with my two dogs at the same time for a simple shampoo wash and nail trim, to avoid any crying from separation. This didn't work out, as they weren't even aware of the appointment, even though it had been booked weeks in advance.

At the wash, I was told they would also apply anti-hair loss conditioner (this is a recurring behavior because the last time I went, it was added to my receipt without my knowledge), even though I hadn't requested it. So I was charged a surcharge twice.

The dogs weren't washed at the same time, resulting in crying. During the wash, I also heard "enough"s addressed to dogs, inappropriately said.

The lady who works at the establishment even went to check on the dog that had been handed in early and was crying, and invited him to go for a nice walk next time (indirectly encouraging me to do so as well).

Finally, the icing on the cake was that she weighed my dog, who weighed exactly 5 kg, on the scale with a harness, two collars, and a leash. Her weight was recorded at 5.1 kg, and she charged me in the 5-15 kg range. The discount on cutting the hind legs, which I wasn't charged, was interesting.

My dog ​​is 10 years old, an Italian champion, always groomed without any problems, but following the death of my longtime groomer, I was looking for a replacement, hopefully worthy. I've always taken dogs to various specialized centers for grooming by appointment. The dog is handed in for the service and picked up afterward.
